bib.title: Coding-agents can replicate scientific machine learning papers

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Coding-agents can replicate scientific machine learning papers", Atharva Hans (Purdue School of Mechanical Engineering; present address Eli Lilly) and Ilias Bilionis (Purdue). arXiv:2607.02134v2 [cs.AI], 10 Jul 2026. Preprint, not peer reviewed. Code and 12 workspaces: github.com/PredictiveScienceLab/paper-replication-paper.

COVERAGE: 16 of 16 pages, all 90,952 chars. I read the body line by line. I skimmed the reference list, which was about 12k chars. There is no appendix. Extraction was clean.

FIT: Section 05 (verification loops) is the best home. It matches your claims on external checks instead of the agent's final message, the definition of done, and separating generation from evaluation. Secondary fit is 06 long-horizon, for state kept in files so the agent can resume after interruptions (the persistent workspace, task ledger and one-active-target rule). It is off-topic for 07 and 08. The fit is conceptual only. The evidence for the effect is weak (see LIMITS).

CORE CLAIM: A prompt does not reliably preserve progress or check evidence. The authors build a coding-agent skill, "Paper-replication", with two mechanisms. The first is a persistent workspace (reproduction matrix, task ledger, run recorder, provenance records). The second is validation checks outside the agent, plus a completion gate. That gate makes "done" a workspace state, not the agent's final message. It is a mechanism and an existence demonstration. It is not a measured improvement.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (one setup throughout: Codex with GPT-5.4 at Extra High reasoning; 4 papers x 3 independent runs = 12 runs; author code disallowed; a queue of 10 follow-up prompts per run; papers are PIFT, PINN-I, PINN-II, SINDy)
- All 12 workspaces pass the completion gate, and all 158 recorded targets reach MATCHED with report coverage. "Matched" is judged under acceptance rules the agent itself records.
- Targets per run: PIFT 8/8/25, PINN-I 8/8/8, PINN-II 9/9/15, SINDy 20/20/20. Decomposition ratio is 3.1 for PIFT and 1.7 for PINN-II.
- Fidelity under fixed paper-anchored thresholds: 37 of 39 scalar anchor-runs (13 anchors x 3 runs) fall inside. Two fall outside but were still MATCHED: Schrödinger run 3 has L2 error 4.8e-2 against a 1% threshold, and Navier-Stokes λ2 run 1 has 16.4% error against a 10% threshold. The same Burgers λ2 coefficient error across three runs was 7.3%, 0.14% and 0.014%.
- Effort: observed elapsed time was 1.2 to 13.0 h. Posterior medians are PINN-II 6.9 h, PINN-I 5.0 h, PIFT 2.2 h and SINDy 1.9 h. 25 executions were superseded (PINN-I 11, PINN-II 10, PIFT 3, SINDy 1). One PINN-I run had 71 tracked executions, 11 superseded.
- Judgment variation: runs chose the same acceptance-rule type for 19/20 SINDy claims, 8/11 PIFT, 4/8 PINN-I and 5/11 PINN-II.
- Cost in dollars or tokens is not reported. Hardware was an M4 Max MacBook plus the Purdue Gautschi cluster (H100 GPUs); the agent chose local or cluster per job.

ABLATION: None. The authors say so explicitly.

QUOTES
1. p.1 abstract: "Paper-replication makes completion depend on workspace evidence and validation checks rather than on the agent's final message."
2. p.2: "A prompt that asks the agent to finish the replication can then lead it to report completion before the workspace contains the required target-level evidence". The paper cites Manheim and Garrabrant 2018 (Goodhart-style gaming).
3. p.4: "An output artifact alone, such as a generated figure or table, does not count as evidence." (Section 2.1)
4. p.13: "It does not include an ablation without the skill, so it characterizes what Paper-replication produces rather than estimating the workflow's effect on an unstructured prompt."

Mechanisms worth teaching, taken from Sections 2.2 and 2.3:
- Acceptance rule written before judging, so it cannot change after a failed comparison.
- Hash checks reject copied paper assets.
- Provenance must link the method to the paper's equations, so a similar-looking substitute method is rejected.
- A validator rejects visual-only evidence for numeric targets.
- Exactly one active target at a time.
- Failed and replaced runs stay in the record.
- Completion gate formula (Eq. 3): all checks pass, every target MATCHED, no active target, report PDF exists.

LIMITS (authors and my reading)
- No no-skill baseline. The paper's motivating claims that prompts alone stop early, lose track and count copied figures are asserted, not measured here.
- Only 4 papers, 3 runs each, and one agent and model. Only 13 scalar anchors, and PIFT has none.
- Completion is relative to the agent's own target list and its own acceptance rules, so "158/158 matched" is partly self-graded. Targets with mismatched scalars still count as matched.
- Each distributional or structural target had one recorded comparison per run. Independent re-judging is future work.
- Hash checks miss transformed copies. The authors observed no such reuse. Passing the checks is "recorded evidence", not proof that the implementation is unique.
- Effort differences are not evidence that PINN papers are harder.
- Scientific-ML domain, and the authors are the tool's developers.

BUILDS ON
- Lopopolo 2026 for "harness engineering".
- Anthropic 2025 and OpenAI 2026 for agent skills.
- Huang et al. 2024 (LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning without external feedback).
- Manheim and Garrabrant 2018 (metric gaming).
- Benchmarks PaperBench (Starace et al. 2025), CORE-Bench (Siegel et al. 2024), PaperCoder (Seo et al. 2025).
- Reproducibility practice from Peng 2011, Sandve et al. 2013, and Stodden et al. 2016.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Fig. 1 (p.3), a three-row diagram of agent work, workspace records, and validation checks ending in the completion gate. It explains the generate/verify separation faster than prose.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The 12 workspaces and the skill are in the authors' GitHub repo, which I did not open.
